definition: llama.cpp is an open-source software library that performs inference on various large language models such as Meta's Llama model.
details: It is co-developed alongside the GGML project, a general-purpose tensor library. Command-line tools are included with the library, alongside a server with a simple web interface. llama.cpp has been considered as the de facto standard as the core of almost all local inference tools, including Ollama and LM Studio.

explainer.lead: How to install Llama.cpp, a first working example, and where it fits in an AI project.
explainer.createdBy: Created by Georgi Gerganov in March 2023; community developed with ggml.ai (now part of Hugging Face).

quickstart.python:
from llama_cpp import Llama

llm = Llama.from_pretrained(
    repo_id="Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct-GGUF",
    filename="*q4_k_m.gguf",
)
out = llm.create_chat_completion(messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Say hi in French."}])
print(out["choices"][0]["message"]["content"])

explainer.inAi: Run quantised GGUF models on a laptop CPU or Apple Silicon with no Python ML stack; many local-AI apps (including Ollama originally) are built on it.

tiers.eli5: It's a lightweight engine that lets a powerful language model run on an ordinary computer, like fitting a big engine into a small car.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use llama.cpp's command-line tools or its server with a simple web interface, often as the core of local inference tools. A pitfall is that running large models locally still depends on available memory and hardware.
tiers.paperLevel: llama.cpp performs inference on various large language models and is co-developed alongside GGML, a general-purpose tensor library. It was created as a pure C/C++ implementation with no dependencies, with strict memory management and multi-threading as design goals.

explainer.example: A developer runs a Llama model on a laptop CPU using llama.cpp's command-line tool to answer prompts without a GPU.
